hero.headline: Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties face millions in property tax losses under state referendum
hero.teaser: A Florida Association of Counties study estimates Martin County could lose $50 million in 2027-28 and $93 million in 2028-29 if voters approve the property tax reform referendum this November.
hero.body:
Government officials are working to assess the impact of the new property tax reform referendum that would raise the homestead exemption and lower property tax bills. A recent study from the Florida Association of Counties offered estimates of potential losses for Treasure Coast counties.

Martin County could lose $50 million in 2027-28 and $93 million in 2028-29. St. Lucie County could lose $80 million in 2027-28 and $140 million in 2028-29. Indian River County could lose $32 million in 2027-28 and $57 million in 2028-29.

Palm Beach County Commissioner Bobby Powell said options like finding new revenue and budget cuts are a possibility. He said officials do not know if it will be an increase in sales tax or an increase in user fees for other services. The referendum to raise the homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 will be decided by voters in November.

cards.headline: Brush fire in Indiantown grows to 125 acres, now 99% contained
cards.teaser: A brush fire that began Friday afternoon in Indiantown escalated to 125 acres before being brought under near-total control by Sunday morning, according to Mart.
cards.body:
A brush fire that began Friday, June 5, in Indiantown escalated over the weekend before being brought under near-total control by Sunday morning. Martin County Fire Rescue firefighters responded to a rapidly developing brush fire in the 2600 block of Southwest Warfield Boulevard just before 3:30 p.m. Crews quickly contained the initial blaze at approximately 37.8 acres, with no reported injuries and no structures threatened. The Florida Forest Service assisted on scene by establishing plow lines to help stop the spread of flames, while Martin County Fire Rescue's drone team identified remaining hotspots and confirmed containment.

By Saturday, June 6, the situation escalated significantly when crews returned to battle a much larger 120-acre brush fire in the same general area. Officials believe the fire rekindled from the previous day's incident. Shifting winds and dense vegetation contributed to rapid fire growth, prompting a large-scale response from Martin County Fire Rescue, the Florida Forest Service, and the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Firefighters worked to protect nearby structures as smoke spread across the area. The fire reached approximately 125 acres in total size and is 99% contained as of Sunday morning. Officials noted early indications suggested the fire may have been a "holdover fire," where a lightning strike could have smoldered underground for days before igniting visible flames. The Florida Forest Service remains in the area monitoring conditions and continues to investigate the fire's origin.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds campaigns in Palm Coast as Democratic gubernatorial field narrows to Jolly
cards.body:
Byron Donalds brought his Defending the Florida Dream tour to Palm Coast on Saturday, focusing on affordability issues while pressing Republicans to unite behind his candidacy for governor. The campaign stop came just as the Democratic primary field contracted significantly. Orange County Mayor Jerry Demings suspended his campaign Friday following a prostate cancer diagnosis, leaving former U.S. Representative David Jolly as the presumptive Democratic nominee. Donalds seized on the development, declaring that the general election has effectively begun. "With the announcement of Jerry Demings dropping out of the Democrat primary for Governor, the general election starts today," Donalds said.

On the trail in Flagler County, Donalds emphasized his affordability message, contrasting his approach with what he characterized as the status quo on cost of living. He pledged to reduce regulatory burdens that he argues are driving up prices for Floridians. "Across the state, Floridians are telling me the same thing: they want Florida to remain Florida," Donalds said. "I'm fighting everyday to make sure everyone has a shot at living the Florida Dream." The campaign described the Palm Coast event as drawing a large and energetic crowd. Press Secretary Skylar Swanson characterized the turnout as evidence of campaign momentum. "The energy in Palm Coast tonight was undeniable, this is what a winning campaign looks like," Swanson said, pointing to Trump's endorsement and Donalds' substantial polling lead of more than 40 points in multiple surveys.

With $81 million raised and a commanding position in the race, Donalds has decided to focus his resources on the general election rather than the primary. He plans to reach voters through town halls, community meetings, business roundtables, and door-to-door canvassing instead of debate stages. Donalds argues that continued Republican infighting with more than two months remaining before the August 18 primary only benefits Democrats. His strategy reflects confidence in his frontrunner status and desire to preserve resources for the general election matchup.

His remaining primary opponents reject this approach. Jay Collins and former House Speaker Paul Renner both are demanding debates. Collins launched The Collins Callout on Friday, a website acknowledging Donalds' commanding frontrunner position while challenging him to participate in debates. "The callout is on the table, the only question left is whether Byron answers the bell, or keeps running," the site states. Renner went further in a video posted to social media, calling on both candidates to stop avoiding the debate stage. "Floridians deserve to see the differences between the candidates," Renner said. Fundraising reports through May, due June 10, will reveal how much fight remains in Collins and Renner's campaigns, with Renner having raised more than $6 million and Collins roughly $1.75 million through March.

cards.headline: Indiantown brush fire grows to 125 acres over weekend, now 99% contained
cards.body:
A brush fire that started Friday in Indiantown spread significantly over the weekend before crews brought it under control, according to Martin County Fire Rescue and the Florida Forest Service. The fire ultimately consumed approximately 125 acres and reached 99% containment by Sunday morning.

The initial incident occurred on Friday, June 5, when Martin County Fire Rescue responded to a rapidly developing brush fire in the 2600 block of Southwest Warfield Boulevard shortly before 3:30 p.m. Firefighters quickly contained this first blaze at approximately 37.8 acres with no injuries reported and no structures threatened. The Florida Forest Service assisted by establishing plow lines to prevent the flames from spreading further. Martin County Fire Rescue's drone team proved instrumental in the operation by locating remaining hotspots and verifying that containment was complete before crews left the scene.

The situation took a dramatic turn on Saturday, June 6, when crews discovered a much larger 120-acre brush fire in the same general area. Officials believe this fire rekindled from the previous day's incident. Rapid fire growth resulted from shifting winds and dense vegetation in the region, prompting a large-scale response involving Martin County Fire Rescue, the Florida Forest Service, and the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Firefighters focused on protecting nearby structures while smoke blanketed the area. Despite the smoke, officials stated there was no broader public threat, though residents were warned to expect smoky conditions throughout the weekend as suppression operations continued.

The cause of the fire remains unknown, though preliminary indications point toward a holdover fire, where a lightning strike may have smoldered underground for several days before emerging as visible flames. The Florida Forest Service continues investigating the fire's origin. The agency has maintained a presence in the area following containment to monitor for any additional flare-ups and ensure the situation remains under control.

cards.headline: Oliver Gilbert to launch congressional campaign in Miami Gardens, setting up primary with Shevrin Jones
cards.teaser: Miami-Dade Commissioner Oliver Gilbert III will formally launch his campaign for Florida's 24th Congressional District on Sunday at Antioch Missionary Baptist Church in Miami Gardens.
cards.body:
Miami-Dade Commissioner Oliver Gilbert III will formally launch his congressional campaign Sunday at 10 a.m. at Antioch Missionary Baptist Church in Miami Gardens, the city where he was born, raised, and twice elected mayor. The announcement caps a week in which he resigned his county seat, filed his Statement of Candidacy with the Federal Election Commission, and launched a campaign website. Gilbert, 53, led Miami Gardens as mayor from 2012 to 2020 before winning a Miami-Dade Commission seat in District 1, where he served as Commission Chair from 2022 to 2024. A Florida A&M University graduate with a law degree from the University of Miami, he resigned from the Commission effective Jan. 3, the day a new member of Congress would be sworn in.

Gilbert is entering a fast-forming field for Florida's 24th Congressional District, following Rep. Frederica Wilson's announcement that she would not seek a ninth term. The marquee matchup is shaping up against state Sen. Shevrin Jones, a fellow Miami Gardens Democrat preliminarily viewed as the early front-runner. Jones, 42, filed his own paperwork Thursday and is a Miami Gardens native, former chair of the Miami-Dade Democratic Party, and a 14-year legislative veteran. The qualifying deadline is June 12, followed by the Aug. 18 Democratic primary and the Nov. 3 general election.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce pastor charged with child neglect after children found in deplorable conditions

cards.body:
A Fort Pierce pastor has been charged with child neglect after children in her care were found living in deplorable conditions, according to authorities. The arrest was made Saturday.

The charges stem from conditions discovered when officials intervened in the care situation. The pastor was taken into custody on child neglect charges related to the youngsters under her supervision.

The investigation remains ongoing as authorities work to determine the full extent of the neglect allegations.

hero.headline: 35 foster youth graduate at ChildNet celebration at Palm Beach State College
hero.teaser: Thirty-five students walked across the stage at ChildNet's annual graduation celebration at Palm Beach State College, marking a milestone for foster youth served by the Broward and Palm Beach County nonprofit.
hero.body:
Thirty-five foster youth and young adults crossed the graduation stage at ChildNet's annual celebration held at Palm Beach State College, marking an important achievement for the Broward and Palm Beach County nonprofit. ChildNet provides comprehensive support to foster children and young adults through education programs, adoption services and independent living resources designed to help them succeed.

Two graduates who exemplified the organization's impact were Sabrina Diaz and Brian Saintfort, both of whom experienced the loss of a parent and sought assistance from ChildNet during difficult times. The organization provided them with the tools and guidance necessary to navigate their circumstances and continue forward with their lives. At the celebration, both young adults shared messages of hope and perseverance with others facing similar challenges. Diaz encouraged those in her situation to maintain faith in their future potential and commit to their education regardless of obstacles. "Belief that you're going to be big one day and just put effort into it, never give up on school and never give up on dreams. If you like push past with the pain and just keep trying hard," she said. Saintfort offered similar encouragement, emphasizing the importance of self-belief. "Believe that you'll make it, then you're gonna make it and stuff," he said.

Larry N. Rein, CEO of ChildNet, spoke about the significance of the evening's celebration. He recognized that the graduates' success reflected the collaborative efforts of many people throughout the community, including case workers from both ChildNet and the Department of Children and Families. Rein emphasized that the young graduates themselves deserved particular credit for their hard work and determination in overcoming the challenges they faced.

Both graduates are moving forward with ambitious plans for their futures. Diaz has already enrolled in pre-med courses at Palm Beach State College with aspirations of becoming a physician. Saintfort is pursuing vocational training to become a plumber. Their forward momentum and clear goals demonstrate the real-world impact of ChildNet's support services on the young people they serve.

cards.headline: Indian River, Martin and St. Lucie counties fertilizer ban takes effect June 1
cards.teaser: Indian River, Martin and St. Lucie counties have a ban on any fertilizer containing phosphorus or nitrogen that runs through September 30.
cards.body:
Starting June 30, residents of Indian River, Martin and St. Lucie counties must stop using fertilizers containing phosphorus or nitrogen on their lawns and landscaping. Jordan Skaggs, with Environmental Resources in St. Lucie County, explained that the ban aims to reduce nutrient-rich runoff during the rainy season, which can cause algae blooms that disrupt waterways like the Indian River Lagoon and St. Lucie River. According to Skaggs, harmful algae blooms can shade out beneficial plants that fish and wildlife depend on and, at certain densities, can release toxins affecting human health, wildlife health and overall ecosystem health.

Grantly Ricketts, director of University of Florida's Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences St. Lucie County Extension, recommends composting as an alternative during the ban period. Ricketts described composting as a practical solution, comparing it to a small trash can and calling it "the easiest and most practical way or means to add nutrients to your landscape."

cards.headline: Florida voters divided on property tax ballot measure ahead of November vote
cards.teaser: Florida voters will decide this November whether to roll back property taxes by raising the homestead exemption for homeowners, a proposal drawing mixed reactions in West Palm Beach.
cards.body:
Florida voters will decide this November whether to raise the homestead exemption to roll back property taxes, a proposal drawing mixed reactions from West Palm Beach residents. The ballot measure requires 60% approval to pass. A similar proposal failed in 2018.

Rosabella Olivares, a shopper in West Palm Beach, expressed concern about reduced funding, saying "there's going to be less money because everything is expensive now." Brian Edington supports the idea because it benefits permanent Florida homeowners and said he is comfortable with local governments spending less. He pointed to his own neighborhood as an example, noting his trash services pick up twice weekly when once a week would be adequate. A resident named Stan said he does not want funding eliminated entirely, stating "infrastructure and all that stuff is important, but if they can lower it to help the people out some." While homeowners were generally supportive of paying less in taxes, renters expressed skepticism. One renter along Clematis Avenue in downtown West Palm Beach said the savings would not reach them, stating "pretty sure they're going to raise the rent on everybody, all the renters."

cards.headline: Palm Beach County rental assistance overwhelmed as demand far outweighs resources
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County's Emergency Rental Assistance Program receives nearly 8,000 calls for housing assistance per month, with about 600 applications flooding in within the first couple hours applications open.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County's Community Services Department has nearly $2 million in combined grant funding for its Emergency Rental Assistance Program, designed to help residents who can't pay rent. However, demand dramatically outpaces available resources. Program director Dr. James Green said the county receives nearly 8,000 calls for housing assistance per month, with about 800 applications currently in the queue for rental assistance. Typically, about 600 applications arrive within the first couple of hours after the portal opens at the beginning of each month. At the time of reporting, the county's assistance portal was marked closed due to high demand. Green urges anyone in need to call 1-833-CSD-WILL to check for availability.

Rising costs of living have fueled the surge in applications. According to the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the average rent for a one-bedroom in Palm Beach County is $2,020 a month. Joanne Bromfield, who recently moved to West Palm Beach from Tampa, said rent is very expensive and she had to switch careers from education to real estate hoping for a higher income. She worries about paying rent almost every day because all bills are rising except paychecks. Green emphasized the importance of keeping residents housed so they can continue working and supporting the economy.

cards.headline: Florida dive operators fight federal shark feeding ban, cite conservation record
cards.teaser: A federal proposal to ban shark feeding off Florida's coast within 200 miles is drawing criticism from shark diving operators who warn it could devastate conservation-driven tourism businesses.
cards.body:
The Safe Florida Seas Act, H.R. 3831, cleared the U.S. House and would prohibit shark feeding in federal waters within 200 miles of Florida, with an exception for harvesting. Supporters call it a common-sense safety measure to reduce human-shark interactions. However, a coalition of dive operators argues the bill unfairly targets their work, often veteran-owned small businesses and nonprofits focused on education, conservation and responsible encounters with sharks, while leaving fishing practices untouched. Nathan Campbell, owner of Emerald Charters, said operators have not been asked by Congress to present data or explain their practices. Dive operators say they avoid surface chumming, instead taking bait underwater during dives, which they argue is less likely to condition sharks to approach boats looking for food, unlike some commercial harvesting operations that can release hundreds of gallons of chum at the surface.

The bill cites Hawaii's 2006 ban on baited shark diving in federal waters as precedent. However, Florida operators and some researchers say the Hawaii experience tells a different story. Dr. Matt Ajemian, an associate research professor at Florida Atlantic University, says shark diving in Florida has a near perfect safety record for customers. Industry members note that since Hawaii's ban, shark incidents have increased and fatalities have been reported. According to the Western Pacific Regional Fishery Management Council, at least one in four fishing trips ends with a shark biting off part of the catch.

cards.headline: Jupiter Island erosion threatens to split barrier island in half, state report warns
cards.teaser: A new state report warns that nearly the entire 11.5-mile coastline of Jupiter Island is critically eroded, with the ocean threatening to breach at Peck Lake and potentially split the island in two.
cards.body:
The 2025 Florida Department of Environmental Protection report found Jupiter Island's 11.5-mile shoreline has eroded so severely the ocean could break through at Peck Lake, potentially splitting the island in half. A storm breached Peck Lake in the early 1960s before the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers filled it back in with sand. The threat stretches from Blowing Rocks Preserve to Peck Lake, where a breach could turn a thin strip of land into an open inlet. Mark Perry with the Florida Oceanographic Society said a future breach could upend ecosystems that depend on a delicate balance of fresh and saltwater to survive.

Among the areas at risk is the Joseph Reed Mound, a 3,000- to 4,000-year-old archaeological site the report says is already half lost to erosion, along with wildlife refuges like Blowing Rocks Preserve, Hobe Sound Wildlife Refuge, and St Lucie Inlet Preserve State Park. Over 33 threatened and endangered species live in those areas. Jupiter Island Commissioner Marshall Field said the town continues to fight erosion through constant maintenance. In April 2025, the town completed a major beach renourishment project, dumping enough sand to fill nearly 400 Olympic-sized swimming pools. About $3 million in town taxpayer dollars goes toward beach renourishment every year. Field said if funding for beach renourishment goes away, the coastline of Florida will change very quickly.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie man arrested after homeowner spots burglary on security camera
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie man was arrested after a homeowner spotted a burglary in progress on a security camera.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie man was taken into custody Saturday after a homeowner watching a security camera feed spotted a burglary taking place at their residence. The arrest followed the real-time observation of the crime.

The homeowner contacted authorities after witnessing the break-in through their security system, leading to a rapid response and the suspect's apprehension. The man now faces burglary charges.

The incident highlights the role of home security systems in helping law enforcement respond to property crimes as they occur.

cards.body:
A man faces charges after he allegedly chased children on bicycles while wielding a baseball bat, according to law enforcement. The incident occurred Saturday and led to his arrest.

Authorities responded to reports of the threatening behavior involving the juvenile cyclists. The man was taken into custody following the incident.

The arrest came after witnesses reported the man pursuing the children in a menacing manner while carrying the bat.

cards.teaser: A masked intruder was arrested following a Port St. Lucie apartment break-in in which a $300 watch was stolen.
cards.body:
A masked suspect was arrested Saturday following a break-in at a Port St. Lucie apartment where a watch valued at $300 was stolen. The incident was captured on video.

The intruder allegedly forced entry into the apartment and took the watch before fleeing the scene. Law enforcement located and arrested the suspect after the burglary.

The arrest follows the apartment break-in that left the victim without the valuable timepiece. The suspect now faces burglary charges in connection with the theft.

cards.body:
A person identifying as a sovereign citizen was taken into custody Saturday following a disturbance at a Florida Walmart. The incident led to law enforcement intervention and the individual's arrest.

Sovereign citizens typically reject government authority and often clash with law enforcement during routine encounters. The arrest followed the disruption at the retail location.

The shooting led to the suspect's arrest and the filing of attempted murder charges. Law enforcement responded to the scene and took the man into custody.

The investigation into the shooting continues as prosecutors prepare the attempted murder case against the accused.

cards.headline: Okeechobee County woman sues Campbell Soup and Walmart over alleged worms in SpaghettiOs
cards.teaser: Mary Hubbard from Okeechobee County says she and her daughter found live worms in SpaghettiOs bought at the Walmart Supercenter on South Parrott Avenue in Okeechobee and is now suing for $50,000.
cards.body:
A woman from Okeechobee County is suing Campbell Soup Co. and Walmart after she and her daughter allegedly found live worms in their SpaghettiOs. Mary Hubbard claims she and her daughter developed parasitic infections and other medical complications following the incident. She purchased the SpaghettiOs in June 2024 at the Walmart Supercenter store on South Parrott Avenue in Okeechobee.

According to the lawsuit, Hubbard discovered what appeared to be worms or parasites actively moving within the food. She documented the contamination in multiple videos that clearly depict worm-like organisms moving within the food product. The lawsuit alleges the companies failed to properly inspect the product and seeks $50,000 in damages. Campbell Soup Co. said the claims lack merit, and Walmart said it is reviewing the court filing.

Supporters have called it a common-sense safety measure to reduce human-shark interactions, citing Hawaii's 2006 ban on baited shark diving as precedent.

A coalition of dive operators says the bill unfairly targets their work while leaving fishing practices untouched. Nathan Campbell, owner of Emerald Charters, said no one from Congress has yet asked operators to present data or explain their practices. Operators say they avoid surface chumming, instead taking bait underwater during dives, which they argue is less likely to condition sharks to approach boats than some commercial harvesting operations that can release hundreds of gallons of chum at the surface. Dr. Matt Ajemian, an associate research professor at Florida Atlantic University, says shark diving in Florida has a "near perfect safety record" for customers. Campbell is urging senators to delay action, gather research and involve all stakeholders in shaping any new rules.

cards.headline: Indian River Mall demolition begins to make way for 300,000 square foot mixed-use development in Vero Beach
cards.body:
Demolition of the Indian River Mall began this week as crews started removing the Macy's building and former Sears location. Joseph Scarfone, the project manager overseeing the redevelopment, said these structures represent the first phase of the revitalization effort.

Neighbors gathered to watch the demolition work. Mary Alice Stopyra, a nearby resident, expressed support for the project, saying the mall had degraded over time. Mark Manera, a Vero Beach resident who had visited the mall for years, described it as resembling "a graveyard" and noted a steady decline year after year. Despite the mall's deterioration, Manera said the redevelopment could bring positive change: "If that brings new life, new jobs, new opportunity, that's wonderful." Scarfone said the site will be transformed into a sleek and modern indoor and outdoor shopping center featuring approximately 300,000 square feet of retail, restaurants, and possible residential spaces. He stated residents will no longer see "a dead mall for the last 12 years that was getting cobwebs," describing the new development as "a city within a city." The project manager hopes the first phase will be completed by 2027, with crews still working on permitting for the remaining phases.

hero.headline: 35 foster youth graduate at ChildNet celebration at Palm Beach State College
hero.teaser: 35 students walked across the stage at ChildNet's annual graduation celebration at Palm Beach State College, marking a milestone for foster youth served by the Broward and Palm Beach County nonprofit.
hero.body:
Thirty-five foster youth and young adults celebrated a significant milestone as they walked across the stage at ChildNet's annual graduation event held at Palm Beach State College. The ceremony honored students served by the nonprofit organization, which operates across Broward and Palm Beach counties. ChildNet provides comprehensive support to foster children and young adults through education programs, adoption services, and independent living resources designed to help them build successful futures.

Among those recognized were Sabrina Diaz and Brian Saintfort, two graduates who each experienced the loss of a parent and sought assistance from ChildNet during difficult times. The organization provided them with essential resources and guidance that enabled them to overcome their challenges and move forward. Diaz offered encouragement to others facing similar circumstances, sharing her perspective on perseverance. "Belief that you're going to be big one day and just put effort into it, never give up on school and never give up on dreams. If you like push past with the pain and just keep trying hard," she said. Saintfort reinforced this message of determination, stating, "Believe that you'll make it, then you're gonna make it and stuff."

Larry N. Rein, CEO of ChildNet, emphasized the importance of the evening's celebration and acknowledged the contributions of everyone involved in supporting these young people. "This evening is the fruition of great work by everyone in the community, including case workers at ChildNet, DCF and especially the kids who have worked so hard. We are to celebrate them!" Rein said. His remarks highlighted the collaborative effort required to help foster youth succeed, recognizing both the dedicated professionals and the resilience of the graduates themselves.

The two featured graduates are already pursuing their professional ambitions. Diaz has enrolled in pre-med courses at Palm Beach State College as she works toward her goal of becoming a physician. Saintfort is pursuing vocational training to become a plumber. Their clear career paths and continued educational engagement demonstrate the positive outcomes that ChildNet's support has helped facilitate for young people in the foster care system.

cards.headline: Martin County could lose $50 million under property tax referendum
cards.teaser: Martin County officials are working to assess the impact of a new property tax reform referendum that would raise the homestead exemption and lower property tax bills.
cards.body:
A recent study from the Florida Association of Counties estimated potential revenue losses for Treasure Coast counties if voters approve the property tax referendum in November. Martin County could lose $50 million in 2027-28 and $93 million in 2028-29. St. Lucie County could lose $80 million in 2027-28 and $140 million in 2028-29. Indian River County could lose $32 million in 2027-28 and $57 million in 2028-29. Okeechobee County could lose $4 million in 2027-28 and $7 million in 2028-29.

The referendum would raise the homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. Homeowner savings can vary from hundreds to thousands of dollars depending on county, city, and home assessed value. Republican lawmakers, including Gov. Ron DeSantis, argue local governments collect too much tax revenue and spend excessively. State Rep. Toby Overdorf, R-Stuart, said the proposal benefits struggling families in homes valued around $300,000. Local officials are restricted by state law from speaking against or endorsing the referendum but can provide educational information about its potential impacts.

cards.headline: Florida voters divided on property tax proposal ahead of November vote
cards.teaser: Florida voters will decide this November whether to roll back property taxes by raising the homestead exemption for homeowners.
cards.body:
Florida voters will decide this November whether to raise the homestead exemption to roll back property taxes, a proposal drawing mixed reactions from West Palm Beach residents. The ballot measure needs 60% approval to pass. A similar proposal to raise the homestead exemption failed in 2018.

Homeowners expressed general support for the proposal. Brian Edington said he supports the idea because it benefits people who permanently live in Florida. "I think it's a really good idea because it saves the people that really live in Florida, the homeowners," Edington said. He said he is comfortable with local governments having to spend less and pointed to his own neighborhood as an example where cuts could be made, such as reducing trash pickup from twice weekly to once weekly. However, renters expressed skepticism, with one resident saying the savings would not reach them. "Pretty sure they're going to raise the rent on everybody, all the renters, I'm pretty sure they're going to raise those taxes," the renter said.

cards.headline: Indiantown brush fire grows to 125 acres, 99% contained after weekend flare-up
cards.teaser: A brush fire that began Friday in Indiantown escalated over the weekend before being brought under near-total control, according to Martin County Fire Rescue an.
cards.body:
A brush fire that began Friday in Indiantown escalated over the weekend before being brought under near-total control, according to Martin County Fire Rescue and the Florida Forest Service. The incident started on Friday, June 5, when MCFR firefighters responded to a rapidly developing brush fire in the 2600 block of Southwest Warfield Boulevard just before 3:30 p.m. Crews quickly contained the blaze at approximately 37.8 acres, with no reported injuries and no structures threatened at the time. The Florida Forest Service assisted on scene by establishing plow lines to help stop the spread of flames, while MCFR's drone team identified remaining hotspots and confirmed full containment before crews cleared the area.

By Saturday, June 6, the situation escalated significantly when crews returned to the same general area to battle a much larger 120-acre brush fire. Officials believe the fire rekindled from the previous day's incident, with shifting winds and dense vegetation contributing to rapid fire growth. This prompted a large-scale response from MCFR, the Florida Forest Service, and the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Firefighters worked to protect nearby structures as smoke spread across the area, though officials confirmed there was no broader threat to the public. The fire had reached approximately 125 acres total and is 99% contained as of Sunday morning. The Florida Forest Service continues to investigate and monitor conditions in the area.

cards.headline: Boynton Beach mother of two facing eviction while pregnant with twins
cards.teaser: A 27-year-old single mother of two in East Boynton Beach is facing eviction while pregnant with twins and placed on strict bed rest.
cards.body:
Chellizabeth Colon, 27, split from her husband three weeks ago. He used to pay the bills. Since then, she has fallen into a financial crisis and can no longer afford her rent on her East Boynton Beach home. When asked if she has heard from her landlord about when she must leave, her response was sobering. "I was supposed to leave yesterday," she said. Adding to the stress, Colon's doctor has placed her on strict bed rest due to placenta previa, a serious pregnancy complication. "I can't really do anything, I wasn't supposed to pack up this whole house by myself, or my water could literally break," she explained.

Colon is a single mother of two daughters, ages 4 and 5, and is expecting twins due in August. She said she has reached out to shelters for help, but they just don't have any availability. "I'm really trying to get some help as much as I can and I can't seem to find it nowhere," she said. After hearing her story, WPTV connected Colon with The Lord's Place, a local nonprofit experiencing a huge need for housing in Palm Beach County. Staff from their housing services said they will be calling Colon directly. Palm Beach County's Community Services Department said Colon may qualify for homeless prevention assistance, depending on her circumstances and whether space is available.

hero.headline: Crossing for Cystic Fibrosis brings 80-mile ocean paddle to Lake Worth Beach June 13
hero.teaser: More than 100 paddlers will cross 80 miles of the open Atlantic Ocean this June to raise awareness and funds for families living with cystic fibrosis in the ann.
hero.body:
More than 100 paddlers will cross 80 miles of the open Atlantic Ocean this June to raise awareness and funds for families living with cystic fibrosis in the annual Crossing for Cystic Fibrosis. According to event founder Travis Suit, participants will launch from Bimini, Bahamas, at midnight on June 13, arriving at Lake Worth Beach after 12 to 16 hours of paddling. The endurance trek benefits the Pipers Angels Foundation, which Suit established in honor of his daughter, Piper, diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at age 4.

The crossing is part of a four-day schedule, beginning June 10, with arrivals and a poolside social at Bimini Cove. On Thursday, participants take part in a 4Ocean beach cleanup and a community buffet dinner. Friday brings a Paddle Out Rose Ceremony to honor cystic fibrosis warriors, followed by rest and safety checks before launch night. All paddlers are required to wear a U.S. Coast Guard-approved personal flotation device, waterproof whistle, and reflective gear during dark hours. GPS trackers provided by the event must be worn and active at all times, and mandatory safety meetings will be held.

The fundraiser expects participants from around the world. Paddlers must raise at least $2,000 for the cause, and crew or virtual participants have a $500 minimum. Final contributions are due July 31. Suit, an avid paddler, was inspired to create the event after learning about the natural respiratory benefits of ocean salt air. The foundation has since grown to provide direct support for cystic fibrosis patients and families, connecting them with resources and community.

Spectators are invited to Lake Worth Beach on June 13 to cheer paddlers during a daylong beach celebration marking their arrival. Cystic fibrosis is a life-shortening genetic condition that affects the lungs and digestive system. More information, registration, and donation details are available at crossingforcysticfibrosis.com and pipersangels.org.

cards.headline: Beetlejuice musical closes final performances today at West Palm Beach Kravis Center
cards.teaser: The Broadway hit wraps its June 2 through June 7 run at the Alexander W. Dreyfoos Concert Hall with a closing matinee performance.
cards.body:
The Broadway production of "Beetlejuice" closes its run at the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach today with a final matinee performance. Running from June 2 through June 7 at the Alexander W. Dreyfoos Concert Hall, the musical has delivered its signature blend of spooky humor, elaborate visuals, and heartwarming moments to Palm Beach County audiences. Actor Ryan Stajmiger performs in the iconic striped suit as Beetlejuice, the mischievous demon character from Tim Burton's 1988 film. The musical follows Lydia Deetz, a teenager described as "strange and unusual," whose life changes after meeting two recently deceased neighbors and a trouble-making demon.

Stajmiger highlighted his favorite aspects of performing the role, noting that he frequently breaks the fourth wall to communicate directly with the audience and share moments with them. The actor credited his longtime appreciation for the source material, saying "I've loved the movie since I was a kid. I'm a huge Tim Burton fan, and you know, Michael Keaton's performance is so iconic." Early in the production's engagement, Stajmiger experienced an unexpected on-stage mishap when both wigs came off simultaneously during a wig change, leaving him bald for an entire scene. Rather than breaking character, he adapted and incorporated the moment into his performance. This week's schedule includes shows at 7:30 p.m. on June 3 and 4, 8 p.m. on June 5, and matinee and evening performances on June 6. Tickets start at $34.50 through kravis.org. The show is recommended for ages 13 and up.

hero.headline: Byron Donalds campaigns in Palm Coast as Democratic gubernatorial field narrows to Jolly
hero.body:
Byron Donalds brought his Defending the Florida Dream tour to Palm Coast on Saturday, focusing on affordability issues while pressing Republicans to unite behind his candidacy for governor. The campaign stop came just as the Democratic primary field contracted significantly. Orange County Mayor Jerry Demings suspended his campaign Friday following a prostate cancer diagnosis, leaving former U.S. Representative David Jolly as the presumptive Democratic nominee. Donalds seized on the development, declaring that the general election has effectively begun. "With the announcement of Jerry Demings dropping out of the Democrat primary for Governor, the general election starts today," Donalds said.

On the trail in Flagler County, Donalds emphasized his affordability message, contrasting his approach with what he characterized as the status quo on cost of living. He pledged to reduce regulatory burdens that he argues are driving up prices for Floridians. "Across the state, Floridians are telling me the same thing: they want Florida to remain Florida," Donalds said. "I'm fighting everyday to make sure everyone has a shot at living the Florida Dream." The campaign described the Palm Coast event as drawing a large and energetic crowd. Press Secretary Skylar Swanson characterized the turnout as evidence of campaign momentum. "The energy in Palm Coast tonight was undeniable, this is what a winning campaign looks like," Swanson said, pointing to Trump's endorsement and Donalds' substantial polling lead of more than 40 points in multiple surveys.

With $81 million raised and a commanding position in the race, Donalds has decided to focus his resources on the general election rather than the primary. He plans to reach voters through town halls, community meetings, business roundtables, and door-to-door canvassing instead of debate stages. Donalds argues that continued Republican infighting with more than two months remaining before the August 18 primary only benefits Democrats. His strategy reflects confidence in his frontrunner status and desire to preserve resources for the general election matchup.

His remaining primary opponents reject this approach. Jay Collins and former House Speaker Paul Renner both are demanding debates. Collins launched The Collins Callout on Friday, a website acknowledging Donalds' commanding frontrunner position while challenging him to participate in debates. "The callout is on the table, the only question left is whether Byron answers the bell, or keeps running," the site states. Renner went further in a video posted to social media, calling on both candidates to stop avoiding the debate stage. "Floridians deserve to see the differences between the candidates," Renner said. Fundraising reports through May, due June 10, will reveal how much fight remains in Collins and Renner's campaigns, with Renner having raised more than $6 million and Collins roughly $1.75 million through March.

cards.headline: Oliver Gilbert to launch congressional campaign in Miami Gardens, setting up primary with Shevrin Jones
cards.teaser: Miami-Dade Commissioner Oliver Gilbert III will formally launch his campaign for Florida's 24th Congressional District on Sunday at Antioch Missionary Baptist Church in Miami Gardens.
cards.body:
Miami-Dade Commissioner Oliver Gilbert III will formally launch his congressional campaign Sunday at 10 a.m. at Antioch Missionary Baptist Church in Miami Gardens, the city where he was born, raised, and twice elected mayor. The announcement caps a week in which he resigned his county seat, filed his Statement of Candidacy with the Federal Election Commission, and launched a campaign website. Gilbert, 53, led Miami Gardens as mayor from 2012 to 2020 before winning a Miami-Dade Commission seat in District 1, where he served as Commission Chair from 2022 to 2024. A Florida A&M University graduate with a law degree from the University of Miami, he resigned from the Commission effective Jan. 3, the day a new member of Congress would be sworn in.

Gilbert is entering a fast-forming field for Florida's 24th Congressional District, following Rep. Frederica Wilson's announcement that she would not seek a ninth term. The marquee matchup is shaping up against state Sen. Shevrin Jones, a fellow Miami Gardens Democrat preliminarily viewed as the early front-runner. Jones, 42, filed his own paperwork Thursday and is a Miami Gardens native, former chair of the Miami-Dade Democratic Party, and a 14-year legislative veteran. The qualifying deadline is June 12, followed by the Aug. 18 Democratic primary and the Nov. 3 general election.

cards.headline: Lauren Book clears Democratic path to return to Florida Senate as Dan Daley exits race
cards.teaser: Former Senate Democratic Leader Lauren Book appears headed for an uncontested Democratic primary in Senate District 30 after Dan Daley announced he would not run.
cards.body:
Lauren Book, who served in the Florida Senate from 2016 to 2024 before term limits forced her out, announced her campaign for Senate District 30 after outgoing Sen. Tina Polsky confirmed she would not seek re-election. Dan Daley, who had been weighing the race seriously for weeks, announced Tuesday he would not run, effectively handing Book an uncontested path to the Democratic nomination. Book, who served as Senate Democratic Leader during her previous tenure, now faces what appears to be an easy trek back to the chamber.

Qualifying begins this week and closes June 12. Republican Jerusa Zitta remains the only other active candidate in the race. The general election will take place Nov. 3. Book walked 1,500 miles this year for her annual Walk in My Shoes event, and her road back to the Senate is shaping up to be an easy trek after clearing the Democratic primary field this week.

cards.headline: Former Lake County Property Appraiser Carey Baker files for Congress, faces Sabatini in Republican primary
cards.teaser: Former Lake County Property Appraiser Carey Baker has filed to succeed retiring U.S. Rep. Dan Webster in Congressional District 11, setting up a Republican primary against Lake County Commissioner Anthony Sabatini.
cards.body:
Former Lake County Property Appraiser Carey Baker has filed to run for Congress in District 11, setting up a Republican primary against Lake County Commissioner Anthony Sabatini, who entered the race within hours of incumbent Dan Webster's retirement announcement. The 63-year-old Baker, a lifelong Eustis resident, represented much of the Central Florida district in both the House and Senate before his election as Property Appraiser. He won his House seat in 2000 and later advanced to the Senate. Baker lost his re-election bid in 2024 after filing as a write-in candidate to avoid the qualifying fee, a strategy that collapsed when Mark Jordan filed as a Republican. Jordan won the general election by a 3-to-1 margin. Despite the loss, Baker demonstrated significant fundraising capacity, raising roughly $233,000 in the 2024 race.

Congressional District 11 encompasses all of Sumter County, part of west Orange County, and most of Lake County, with more than 57 percent of voters backing President Donald Trump in the 2024 presidential election. The Democratic field lost its presumptive frontrunner Saturday when repeat candidate Barbie Harden Hall suspended her campaign due to health issues. Hall was the party's 2024 nominee and the leading Democratic fundraiser this cycle. Three other Democratic candidates remain in the running: Royal Webster, Shawn Bettis, and Dan Williams.

cards.headline: Tampa City Council chair seeks delay on Rays stadium vote as CRA negotiations continue
cards.teaser: Tampa City Council Chair Alan Clendenin is pushing to delay a Community Redevelopment Agency discussion tied to the Tampa Bay Rays stadium proposal, saying negotiations continue and the issue is not ready for a vote.
cards.body:
Tampa City Council Chair Alan Clendenin submitted a memo last week requesting that the Rays stadium item be deferred until at least July, and possibly longer, rather than being taken up by the Tampa CRA next week as originally planned. Clendenin disputed remarks made by Hillsborough County Commissioner Joshua Wostal about the status of negotiations and clarified that behind-the-scenes talks are ongoing. He cited recent uncertainty over property tax reform as an additional factor for negotiators to consider.

The Rays stadium memorandum of understanding approved by Tampa and Hillsborough County last month includes $80 million from the city of Tampa and another $100 million tied to the Tampa CRA, in addition to other public dollars. Clendenin said the earlier votes by the City Council and County Commission represented support for the general direction of the non-binding MOU, but not final approval of the CRA terms. Several options remain on the table for the CRA-related portion of the deal, including not using the CRA, creating a different type of district, or using another special district structure. Clendenin stated that nothing has been agreed to by any party regarding the CRA portion and negotiations are continuing behind the scenes.

cards.headline: Jon Maples holds 43-point lead over Jonathan Rubin in House District 87 Republican primary poll
cards.teaser: Former Lake Clarke Shores Town Council member Jon Maples leads opponent Jonathan Rubin 53 percent to 10 percent in the Republican primary for House District 87, a new poll reveals.
cards.body:
Former Lake Clarke Shores Town Council member Jon Maples leads Jonathan Rubin by a wide margin in the GOP Primary for House District 87, according to a poll from Miami-based pollster Inquire, LLC. Maples leads 53% to 10%, with 37% undecided. He performs even stronger among seniors at 58%, high-propensity voters at 60%, and voters who identify strongly as MAGA at 64%. Maples has a 54% favorability rating against 7% unfavorable, while Rubin has a 15% favorability and 5% unfavorable rating. Notably, 51% of respondents have never heard of Rubin, compared to just 11% who don't know who Maples is.

When informed that Maples was recently defeated by Democrat Emily Gregory in a special election for the seat, 63% of respondents say they will still vote for Maples because he ran a strong campaign and only narrowly lost. Just 14% prefer someone else because Maples already lost. Despite the district favoring Democrats, 87% of GOP Primary voters in House District 87 hold a favorable view of President Donald Trump, with 68% calling it "very favorable." The Inquire poll was conducted May 26-28 among 257 likely GOP Primary voters and has a margin of error of 6.1 percentage points. House District 87 runs through Palm Beach Gardens, Jupiter, Juno Beach and Hypoluxo.

cards.headline: University of South Florida President Moez Limayem navigates series of campus crises in opening months
cards.teaser: Moez Limayem became the University of South Florida's ninth President on Feb. 17 and has spent his first 3.5 months navigating a catalog of institutional crises.
cards.body:
University of South Florida President Moez Limayem began his tenure on Feb. 17 and has spent his first 108 days navigating a series of institutional crises. In early April, a suspicious package at Fowler Fields triggered a bomb scare before investigators cleared it as a non-threat. Mid-April brought the disappearance of doctoral students Nahida Bristy and Zamil Limon, both 27-year-old Bangladeshi students from the Tampa area. Limon's roommate, Hisham Abugharbieh, was arrested and charged with two counts of first-degree murder, with prosecutors seeking the death penalty. Limayem spoke at a public vigil, was visibly emotional and told the community he understood the loss as a former international student and father. He promised a comprehensive review of off-campus housing safety and said USF would stop recommending complexes that did not meet standards. This week, the university announced a new off-campus housing provider program.

Days after Bristy's remains were identified, the Marine Science Laboratory at USF's St. Petersburg campus caught fire, with more than 200 firefighters responding. The 80-year-old building, which housed the College of Marine Science's chemistry, biology and oceanography research operations, was declared a total loss. Limayem ran his first commencement ceremonies in early May with two empty chairs on the arena floor during the doctoral ceremony, representing Bristy and Limon, who both received their degrees posthumously. On May 17, 21-year-old honors student Lauryn Akey was killed on Interstate 75 in Charlotte County when an alleged drunk driver made a wrong-way turn. This week, a 21-year-old student identified as Hansel Pearson stabbed his roommate and another person at the Halo 46 Apartments near campus before being found dead hours later at a nearby student housing complex.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast viewing locations recommended for upcoming SpaceX launch
hero.teaser: A guide to the best Treasure Coast locations for watching the next SpaceX launch has been published.
hero.body:
A guide to the best Treasure Coast locations for watching the next SpaceX launch has been published on Sunday, June 7. The recommendations cover viewing spots across Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.

SpaceX launches from Kennedy Space Center are visible from the Treasure Coast, which is located approximately 100 miles south of the launch site. The guide provides options for residents seeking optimal views of rocket launches.

cards.headline: Stuart unveils mural promoting ecosystem awareness
cards.teaser: The city of Stuart unveiled a large-scale mural designed to promote ecosystem awareness.
cards.body:
The city of Stuart unveiled a large-scale mural designed to promote ecosystem awareness on Saturday, June 6. The mural project was completed in the city.

The installation represents part of Stuart's ongoing environmental education initiatives. The artwork is visible to the public in Stuart.

cards.headline: Voting open for best restaurant in Port Salerno area
cards.teaser: A public poll is asking residents to vote for the best restaurant in the Port Salerno area of Stuart.
cards.body:
A public poll is asking residents to vote for the best restaurant in the Port Salerno area of Stuart. The voting campaign was launched on Saturday, June 6.

Port Salerno is located within Stuart's boundaries in southern Martin County. The poll aims to identify the top dining establishment in the waterfront community.

cards.headline: Indiantown brush fire grows to 125 acres, 99% contained after rekindling
cards.teaser: A brush fire that began Friday in Indiantown escalated over the weekend before being brought under near-total control, according to Martin County Fire Rescue an.
cards.body:
A brush fire that began Friday in Indiantown escalated over the weekend before being brought under near-total control, according to Martin County Fire Rescue and the Florida Forest Service. The incident started on Friday, June 5, when firefighters responded to a rapidly developing brush fire in the 2600 block of Southwest Warfield Boulevard just before 3:30 p.m. Crews quickly contained the blaze at approximately 37.8 acres, with no reported injuries and no structures threatened at the time. The Florida Forest Service assisted on scene by establishing plow lines to help stop the spread of flames, while Martin County Fire Rescue's drone team identified remaining hotspots and confirmed full containment.

By Saturday, June 6, crews returned to the same general area to battle a much larger 120-acre brush fire that officials believe rekindled from the previous day's incident. Shifting winds and dense vegetation contributed to rapid fire growth, prompting a large-scale response from Martin County Fire Rescue, the Florida Forest Service, and the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Firefighters worked to protect nearby structures as smoke spread across the area, though officials confirmed there was no broader threat to the public. The fire reached approximately 125 acres in total size and is 99% contained as of Sunday morning. The Florida Forest Service remains monitoring conditions to ensure no further flare-ups occur, and authorities say the investigation into the fire's origin remains ongoing.

cards.headline: Five public dog parks available on Treasure Coast
cards.teaser: A list of five public dog parks across the Treasure Coast has been compiled for pet owners.
cards.body:
A list of five public dog parks across the Treasure Coast has been compiled for pet owners on Sunday, June 7. The parks are located throughout Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.

The dog parks provide designated areas where pets can exercise off-leash. The facilities serve residents seeking outdoor recreation options for their animals.

cards.headline: Poll asks residents to pick restaurant with best gourmet salad
cards.teaser: A voting campaign is seeking public input on which Florida restaurant serves the best gourmet salad.
cards.body:
A voting campaign is seeking public input on which Florida restaurant serves the best gourmet salad, according to a poll launched Sunday, June 7. The poll is open to residents across the state.

The survey aims to identify top restaurants known for their salad offerings. Voting is available to the public.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast beach volleyball players named to all-area team
cards.teaser: The top beach volleyball players from the Treasure Coast have been selected for the spring all-area team.
cards.body:
The top beach volleyball players from the Treasure Coast have been selected for the spring all-area team, announced Sunday, June 7. The honors recognize the best performers from the recent season.

The all-area selections cover athletes from Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties. The recognition highlights high school beach volleyball talent across the region.

hero.headline: Flutie Brothers to perform free concert at Capt. Hiram's Sandbar in Sebastian
hero.teaser: The Flutie Brothers band will perform their annual free concert at Capt. Hiram's Sandbar in Sebastian.
hero.body:
The Flutie Brothers are scheduled to rock Capt. Hiram's Sandbar in Sebastian during their annual free concert appearance. The band, led by former NFL quarterback Doug Flutie and his brother Darren, returns to the popular waterfront venue.

Capt. Hiram's Resort in Sebastian has hosted the Flutie Brothers for their free annual performance, drawing crowds to the Sandbar venue. The event has become a regular attraction at the Indian River County waterfront location.

The concert continues the tradition of live music at Capt. Hiram's Sandbar, which regularly features performances along the Sebastian waterfront. Attendees can expect the band's signature mix of rock and classic covers at the no-admission event.

cards.headline: Texas Rangers Youth Academy team to debut in Vero Beach June 17
cards.teaser: The Texas Rangers Youth Academy 2026 Breakthrough Series Invitational team is set to make its debut in Vero Beach on June 17.
cards.body:
The Texas Rangers Youth Academy 2026 Breakthrough Series Invitational team is set to make its debut in Vero Beach on June 17. The event marks the first appearance for the academy team in the Treasure Coast city.

The Breakthrough Series Invitational provides competitive opportunities for youth baseball players affiliated with Major League Baseball academy programs. The Texas Rangers Youth Academy develops young players through structured training and competitive play.

Vero Beach has a long history with professional baseball, having served as the spring training home for the Los Angeles Dodgers for decades. The city continues to host baseball events at its local facilities.

The June 17 debut will bring the Rangers academy team to Indian River County for the invitational tournament. Details about the specific venue and additional participating teams were not provided in the announcement.

cards.headline: Wildlife scientists report increase in dolphin fishing line entanglements in Indian River Lagoon
cards.teaser: Scientists are expressing concern over a skyrocketing number of dolphins entangled in fishing line in the Indian River Lagoon.
cards.body:
Wildlife scientists have reported a concerning rise in cases of dolphins becoming entangled in fishing line throughout the Indian River Lagoon. The increase in entanglement incidents has prompted heightened attention from researchers monitoring the lagoon's marine life.

The Indian River Lagoon stretches through Indian River County and neighboring areas, serving as critical habitat for bottlenose dolphins and other marine species. Fishing line entanglements pose serious health risks to dolphins, potentially causing injury or death.

Scientists tracking dolphin populations in the lagoon have documented the rising trend in fishing line cases. The lagoon system faces ongoing environmental challenges affecting its wildlife populations.

cards.headline: Recycling Club of Indian River County announces 2026 college scholarship opportunities
cards.teaser: The Recycling Club of Indian River County has announced scholarship opportunities for college students in 2026.
cards.body:
The Recycling Club of Indian River County is offering college scholarship opportunities for 2026. The organization provides financial assistance to students pursuing higher education.

The scholarships are available to eligible students in Indian River County. The Recycling Club focuses on promoting environmental stewardship and education throughout the community.

Students interested in applying for the 2026 scholarships can seek information from the Recycling Club of Indian River County. The organization supports educational advancement for local students through its scholarship program.

cards.headline: Woman's body discovered in Indian River Lagoon
cards.teaser: Authorities found a woman's body in the Indian River Lagoon in Florida.
cards.body:
A woman's body was discovered in the Indian River Lagoon, according to reports. The discovery was made in the lagoon system that runs through multiple counties on Florida's east coast.

The Indian River Lagoon extends through Indian River County and surrounding areas. Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the discovery.

The body was found in the lagoon waters. No additional information about the identity of the woman or the circumstances of the incident was immediately available.

cards.headline: Capt. Hiram's Resort Sandbar in Sebastian marks years of waterfront entertainment
cards.teaser: The Sandbar at Capt. Hiram's Resort in Sebastian has served as a waterfront venue over the years.
cards.body:
The Sandbar at Capt. Hiram's Resort in Sebastian has been a fixture on the Indian River County waterfront. The venue has hosted live music and entertainment events throughout its history.
